Reference / crypto/jwt

crypto/jwt#

JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519) signed as JWS compact serialization (RFC 7515): HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, ES256/384 and EdDSA (Ed25519, RFC 8037).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let key = JwtHmacKey(algorithm: JwtAlgorithm.hs256, secret: secret);
let token = JwtToken(
    claims: Json(JsonField("sub", "user-7"), JsonField("role", "admin")),
    key: key,
    expires: Duration(seconds: (15 * 60).rat())
).string();

let verified = JwtVerified(token: token, key: key, leeway: Duration(seconds: 30.rat()));
verified.claims().text("sub");                       // "user-7"
verified.claims().maybe("role").text() else "user";

Description#

JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519) signed as JWS compact serialization (RFC 7515): HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, ES256/384 and EdDSA (Ed25519, RFC 8037).

The key decides the algorithm, both when signing and when verifying: a token whose alg is not the key's is JwtAlgorithmMismatch, and none is never accepted, so one algorithm cannot stand in for another. exp and nbf are checked whenever they are present (within the leeway), aud and iss when the verifier names them. Several keys go in JwtKeys, chosen by the token's kid. Tokens are at most 8 KiB.

A service that only checks tokens holds the public half: JwtRsaKey, JwtEcdsaKey and JwtEd25519Key take verifying: a public key as well as signing: a private one, and such a key throws JwtKeyCannotSign when asked to sign.

let issuer = JwtEd25519Key(signing: private, id: "2026-11");
let checker = JwtKeys(JwtEd25519Key(verifying: public, id: "2026-11"));
JwtVerified(token: token, keys: checker, issuer: "auth").claims();

Errors#

  • InvalidJwt: not a compact JWS with a JSON header and claims.
  • JwtAlgorithmMismatch: the token's alg is not the key's.
  • JwtSignatureMismatch: the signature does not verify.
  • JwtExpired, JwtNotYetValid: outside exp or nbf (and iat in the future).
  • JwtAudienceMismatch, JwtIssuerMismatch: aud or iss is not the expected one.
  • JwtUnknownKey: no key has the token's kid.
  • InvalidJwtKey: a key that does not fit its algorithm.
  • JwtKeyCannotSign: a verifying key asked to sign.
